subject.title: Feature request: first-class async result routing back to originating topic sessions

question: Should OpenClaw core define a first-class async route registry/API now, or should this remain plugin-owned using existing hooks, wake, delivery-context, and dedupe surfaces until a missing SDK seam is identified?
rationale: The request is a cross-cutting product/API/storage/privacy/safety decision rather than a narrow bug repair, and repository vision favors lean core plus plugin/API seams for optional capability.

options.title: Design plugin/API seam first
options.body: Specify the generic route contract and missing SDK hooks while keeping source watchers and service-specific matchers plugin-owned unless core storage or delivery gaps are proven.

options.title: Build a core Gateway registry
options.body: Core would own route persistence, matching, ambiguity handling, privacy policy, dedupe, delivery, and migration behavior for a first-party framework feature.

options.title: Defer to workspace plugins
options.body: Keep the current low-level primitives only and ask users to build route ledgers in plugins or local automation until stronger demand narrows the core need.

recommendation.title: Design plugin/API seam first
recommendation.body: Specify the generic route contract and missing SDK hooks while keeping source watchers and service-specific matchers plugin-owned unless core storage or delivery gaps are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans product scope, plugin boundaries, storage, and recent wake/dedupe history where steipete has relevant adjacent commits and issue discussion.
